searchText: https://docs.egl.vote/protocol-overview/the-dao/core-devs/allocations <:PeepoDetective:585621159027015680> After the merge, a user running a beacon node or an execution engine, helps the network, even if not validating. What would be preferible given that a user will run one but not both? I thought one has to run both. It would be bundled. Edit: Oh, running one is also helpful? <@!536468500513030147> shorten your message and keep it technical, this is not an advertisement server <@!755590043632140352> They are both important in their own ways for network health, you should run both if you run a validator. Both is always preferred really. I suppose the execution engine, if able to serve and sync on its own, is more valuable for the greater good to run (since there's lots of state to serve to other nodes). If you run an execution client and use a third party consensus client for tracking head, what is the worst that can happen to you? I guess you could get fed a fake chain? The fake chain would need to follow all execution consensus rules, but it may be a fork chain. I guess the consensus client you talk to could also tell you that the chain is finalized (when it isn't). Yeah and the other way around you may not gossip good attestations/blocks which would be the main help of running a node without a vc. But my guess is with proto that the eth1 client is more useful overall. Also it takes much more resources You could still be a transaction relay, though you may slowly fall out of sync and eventually get disconnected as you would broadcast invalid transactions to the network (used nonces and the like). Would be interesting to see a light-client node (Eth2 has good support for that after Altair upgrade) to determine the head, then you can sync an execution node without the consensus node trust assumption Light client consensus, full client execution? yes And the portal network solves the problem the other way I guess An odd pairing since execution is the big one, but I like the general idea of mixing and matching light/heavy like that. A beacon node isn't that heavy to run compared to an exec node though Just netto better than trusting an external consensus API provider Execution is the big one, but consensus is heavy on CPU at prescribed times, which may strain the execution client at those times ``` Consensus | Execution Ideal: Full | Full Good: Light | Full OK: Full | Portal Alright: Light | Portal Meh: Full | External Ugh: Light | External Bad: External | External ``` What is portal for execution? Anywhere I can read up a summary on it? <#796057759858425866> There's the ethcc talk. https://notes.ethereum.org/@pipermerriam/BkiHhhO3d Hello I believe this is off topic, but I am looking to contribute to the development of ethereum and I was wondering if anyone knew how I could do that. I am 19 years old and doing a cs degree, but I am very passionate about this project and just want to contribute to it in any way possible while also honing my coding skills There is an apprenticeship program, though I think it is "between rounds" right now. <@420951281910284289> may have the details? I also to want do ethereum development (But I never actually did anything 🤪 ). I think there could be many directions for projects. Have you decided which part you are most interested about? Honestly I am not sure I am very into consensus but I would also like to do the client side The problem is that I am very into everything 😅 +1. I've had people asking me for that too. Basically the equivalent of "just" running an eth1 node today `s/eth1 node/execution client/` 😉 Piper has been spearheading that, cohort 0 is in full swing, with plans for another cohort in the near future!
